short: Bound the log-weighted sum of twisted cohomology lengths

statements.markdown: Statement 8.1 (VVle, VWin). For the host field E at scale x, with t 0 = ⌊x 401 ⌋ twists, every len ℓ (e) with 1 ≤ e < t 0 is finite and √ X X log ℓ len ℓ (e) ≤ b, b = exp(x ε ), 1≤e<t 0 ℓ for all x in a window [Y 1 , Y 1 2 ]; there is J ≥ 1 such that for every large X such a window lies in [X 1/J , X].

lean.name: UpperTheory.Top.VVle
lean.plain: Bound the log-weighted sum of twisted cohomology lengths
lean.fidelity_note: `VVle E t B` fixes the host field, twist cutoff and upper bound. For each choice of algebraic closure and local data it first requires finite Sha length for every prime and $1\le e<t$, then bounds the sum over each finite set of primes by $B$. The summands are nonnegative, so the supremum of the finite sums is the full sum in the paper. The scale-dependent choices of $t$ and $B$ and the window quantifiers belong to `VAt` and `VWin`.

lean.name: UpperTheory.Top.VWin
lean.plain: Windowed cohomology bounds for every primitive character
lean.note: `VWin` fixes the exponent $401$. For each primitive character, $0<\varepsilon<1/52$ and a function choosing an admissible cyclotomic layer at every $x\ge1$, Lean chooses $J$ and a starting scale $X_0$. For each $X\ge X_0$ and each eligible prime pair at $X^{1/J}$, it then chooses $[Y,Y^2]\subseteq[X^{1/J},X]$. The same pair is used throughout that window, and the bound is required for every matching host field at every scale in it. The paper abbreviates this order of choices.
